dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Pense: quantas vezes o número 7 cabe dentro do 9? Esse valor será o seu número inteiro.
Tente dividir 9 por 7. O quociente vai na parte inteira (m1) e o que sobrar da divisão será o novo numerador (m2).
Se você tirar 7 de 9, quanto sobra? Esse resto é o numerador da sua fração, e o denominador (m3) continua sendo o mesmo da fração original.
Você quase conseguiu! 9 dividido por 7 é 1 com resto 2. Coloque 1 em m1, 2 em m2 e mantenha o 7 em m3.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem? Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you." com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); botão "Convert" que abre as caixas do número misto (m1 = parte inteira, m2/m3 = fração restante; "-" quando não há); reta numérica de 0 a 2 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 7 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

erros.devolutiva: The numerator is the top number of the fraction. The number 7 describes the days in one week, so it belongs in the denominator.
erros.buggyRule: Inverter os valores: colocar o denominador (7) no lugar do numerador e vice-versa.

erros.devolutiva: The denominator represents the equal parts in one week. Since one week has 7 days, use 7 rather than the 2 weeks available.
The denominator keeps the meaning of the equal parts. It remains 7 after conversion and cannot become 0.
The midpoint of the number line is 1.5, but 9/7 is only two sevenths past 1, so it is closer to 1.
erros.buggyRule: Posicionar o ponto sempre no meio (1.5) por ser uma âncora visual comum quando o aluno não sabe estimar.

erros.devolutiva: Count the intervals between marks rather than counting the starting point as an additional interval.

dicas.texto: The numerator tells how many parts of the whole are being counted.
Use the number of days Eric took as the numerator.
Look for the quantity that tells how many days were used.
Type the number of days, 9, in the top fraction box.
The denominator tells how many equal parts make one whole week.
Convert the unit week into its number of equal daily parts.
Use the number of days in one week, not the total number of weeks available.
Type 7 in the bottom fraction box because one week contains 7 days.
Compare the number of counted parts with the number of parts in one whole.
If the numerator is larger than the denominator, the fraction represents more than one whole.
Check whether 9 is larger than 7.
Select the model state that says the fraction is ....
An improper fraction greater than one can be rewritten as whole groups plus a remaining fraction.
Find how many complete groups of 7 fit into 9, then find what remains.
One complete group uses 7 of the 9 parts, leaving 2 parts.
Enter 1 as the whole number, enter 2 as the remaining numerator, and keep 7 as the remaining denominator.
Use the whole-number point 1 as the starting reference.
Divide each unit into seven equal intervals and count the required intervals from 0.
The point is just to the right of 1, not halfway between 1 and 2.
Start at 1 and move two equal seventh intervals to the right, then place the point there.
Before submitting, connect the fraction with its location on the number line.
Check that the point is two seventh intervals to the right of 1.
Make sure the point is not at the midpoint and is aligned with a seventh interval.
When the point shows 9/7, use the Done button to submit the completed activity.

exercicio.statement:
Eric had two weeks to finish a science project. He was able to finish it in only nine days. How would you describe the number of weeks it took him to finish the project? Show the fraction on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem? Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you.

nodes.description: O aluno confunde a posição das grandezas na estrutura da fração.
nodes.instruction: The numerator is the top number of the fraction. The number 7 describes the days in one week, so it belongs in the denominator.

nodes.description: O aluno usa o número de semanas (2) como denominador em vez da unidade de tempo (dias) da semana (7).
nodes.instruction: The denominator represents the equal parts in one week. Since one week has 7 days, use 7 rather than the 2 weeks available.

nodes.description: O aluno tenta converter 9/7 para misto, mas ao subtrair 7 de 9, ele esquece de manter o denominador original na parte fracionária, colocando 0.
nodes.instruction: The denominator keeps the meaning of the equal parts. It remains 7 after conversion and cannot become 0.

nodes.description: O aluno usa a metade da reta como referência padrão para qualquer fração maior que 1.
nodes.instruction: The midpoint of the number line is 1.5, but 9/7 is only two sevenths past 1, so it is closer to 1.

nodes.description: O aluno conta o ponto inicial (0) como a primeira unidade, deslocando o valor para a direita.
nodes.instruction: Count the intervals between marks rather than counting the starting point as an additional interval.
